problems.problem: The revised sentence has two small clarity faults. First, ‘since then few would have remained’ reads first as time (‘since that time’), when it is meant as a condition (had the LORD refined as a silversmith does, few would have remained). Second, ‘the LORD recalls his trials’ follows straight after ‘His name’s sake’, so ‘his’ can be taken for the LORD’s own. The sentence is at the 45-word cap, so a clarifying word cannot simply be added. Radak’s reading itself is accurate (ולא כצורף כסף … יסיר כל הסיגים … כי מעטים היו הנשארים אם עשיתי כן … לא להכריתם מכל וכל).
problems.fix: Drop the aside about the name, name Israel and make the condition explicit. For example: “Midway through rebuking obstinate Jacob, the LORD recalls Israel’s trials; Radak, on 48:10, reads it as a refining short of the refiner’s, who removes all the dross, for had He done so few would have remained, the wicked afflicted but not wholly cut off.” That is 43 words and passes entry-check (scratch/c2/139-fix.json). Leave src unchanged.
